newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - Nov 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- GREYCOAT REJECTS MOORFIELD BID

Greycoat Properties rejected a 200 million stg all-paper takeover proposal from Moorfield Estates. Greycoat, under attack from rebel shareholders to improve its share price performance have considered the offer since Thursday but the board said that the offer was too vague with valuations, contained no cash alternative, would add no value for Greycoat shareholders and show Moorfield lacks experience of prime central London office properties.
-- UNICHEM VOWS TO LIFT LLOYDS PROFITS

Unichem has promised to deliver additional profits of over 20 million stg a year if shareholders in Lloyds Chemists accepts its bid rather than a marginally higher offer from Gehe, its German rival. Unichem chairman, Lord Rippon tells shareholders in a letter they should receive today, that he estimates 15 million stg in additional returns in the first year and more than 20 million stg thereafter.
-- PARKWOOD TO FLOAT WITH 15 MILLION STG TAG

Parkwood Holdings, the facilities management company will have an expected value of 15 million stg when it is priced on Thursday ahead of its London Stock Exchange listing. The group, set up in July 1992, hopes to raise six million stg of new money with the flotation.
THE TIMES
-- COURT LIKELY TO REJECT LIMIT ON BACK VAT

The High Court is expected to rule that Customs & Excise acted illegally in refusing to pay out claims for back dated VAT going back beyond three years. The judicial review of Customs' powers starts tomorrow, with a ruling expected on Thursday. The landmark case could cost the Exchequer up to five billion stg, and the immediate pay out could exceed 100 million stg, should Customs & Excise lose the case.
-- EAST MIDLANDS MAY FACE U.S. BID

Dominion Resources are expected to make a bid for East Midlands Electricity this morning. Last week the American company was forced to disclose an interest in bidding, and last night, at a meeting in Richmond, Virginia, the board were thought to be putting the final touches to their plans. Dominion already has the necessary clearance from its local regulatory authorities to make an offer.
-- BUSINESSES EXPECT SINGLE CURRENCY TO GO AHEAD

In a poll carried out by MORI for the Confederation of British Industry, 87 percent of businesses supported the UK's membership of the European Union, and 56 percent supporting the principle of Britain's participation in a single currency, with 30 percent opposed. Despite the division, leaders of the CBI declared yesterday that a single currency is coming across Europe.
THE GUARDIAN
-- DELAYS COST GEC-ALSTHOM DEAR

GEC-Alsthom, the engineering group, has been forced to pay compensation to PowerGen, the electricity generator, after failing to build a new gas-fired power station on schedule because of technical problems. The Connah's Quay power station in north Wales will be completed by the end of the year, up to two months late.
-- GRANADA'S ONE BLN STG SALE OF EXCLUSIVE HOTELS GROUP HITS SNAG

The sale of Granada's one billion stg Exclusive hotels portfolio may now go on will into next year after negotiations between the company's financial advisers, Lazard Brothers, and would be buyers were inconclusive. Lazard Brothers had hoped to complete the sale by Christmas, but they have struggled to find buyers for some of the less attractive properties in the portfolio causing the delay.
-- CAPITAL TO BUY MY KINDA TOWN

Britain's biggest independent radio group, Capital Radio, is poised to announce the acquisition of My Kinda Town, the restaurant operator, for near to 50 million stg. Capital which is expected to report record full-year pre-tax profits of 30 million stg, already jointly runs the Radio Cafe with My Kinda Town, in London's Leicester, and details of the deal are expected to be announced from the Radio Cafe to analysts tomorrow.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- FRANCE ASKS SFO TO INVESTIGATE EUROTUNNEL SHARES

The Serious Fraud Office has agreed to investigate alleged insider dealing in Eurotunnel shares after Michael Howard, the Home Secretary, received a request from the French authorities. The claims involve insiders profiting from privileged information about the Anglo-French Channel tunnel operation with some eight or nine of Britain's leading banks and financial institutions being at the centre of the probe.
-- CITY TAKES THE PRESSURE OFF PEARSON CHIEFS

The new management at Pearson, the media conglomerate, is to be given a honeymoon period to develop a coherent strategy according to leading City institutions. According to several of the top institutional shareholders, Marjorie Scardino, the chief executive-elect, and Dennis Stevenson, who will take over as chairman next year, will be given the 'benefit of the doubt' as they try to steer the company to a clearer strategy.
-- ITN TO SIGN CUT-PRICE CONTRACT WITH ITV

ITN will this week finally reach agreement on the controversial renewal of its contract to supply ITV with news programmes. ITN, which makes news programmes for Channel 4 and Channel 5 as well as ITV, had been dogged by ownership questions and a putative bid by BSkyB for the ITV contract, will see an end to several years of uncertainty with the signing of the new agreement which will be for five years.
